transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

That duration is normal for an Eco 40-60 programme on modern AEG machines. These cycles are designed to save energy by washing at lower temperatures for longer periods, which typically takes between three and four hours. Your old machine likely used a standard Cottons cycle or heated the water more aggressively to shorten the time. Please confirm that the display shows 'Eco 40-60' specifically, and let me know if the cycle completes successfully after that time.
Yes, it says Eco 40-60 and it does finish and spin, with no error codes. The clothes come out clean too. It just seems a very long time for a 40 wash, so I wanted to be sure it's not a fault.

Since the cycle completes successfully with no errors and your clothes come out clean, this is most likely not a fault. The Eco 40-60 programme is an energy-saving standard that uses lower temperatures for longer periods to reduce electricity use, which naturally extends the wash time to around three or four hours. Your old machine likely used a different cycle logic or heated water more aggressively to finish faster. You do not need to send it back; this duration is normal for this specific programme on modern AEG machines.
